title: Cozy pixel seaside village loop
prompt: Output: one WAV, 48 kHz / 16-bit / stereo, exactly 1,536,000 samples (32.0 s at 30 fps = 960 frames). Python + numpy/scipy only. Synthesise everything (no samples, no downloads, no speech). Fixed random seed (np.random.default_rng(55)). A seamless 32-second cozy pixel-game town loop in G major at 90 BPM (1 beat = 20 frames, 12 bars). Soft chiptune palette: a rounded square lead (25% duty, 3 kHz low-pass, gentle vibrato after 150 ms), triangle bass, a plucked 'kalimba' (Karplus-Strong, short) and a noise-channel shaker on 8ths at low level. Progression Gmaj7 → Em7 → Cmaj7 → D6sus4, 2 bars each, twice, then a 4-bar B section (Am7 → D7 → Bm7 → C6) ; an original, relaxed melody, mostly quarter and dotted notes. Bed of gentle seaside air: faint low-passed wave swells every 8 s (pink noise, 400 Hz low-pass, slow attack). Mono-ish (side/mid ~0.15) like a handheld. The last beat must flow into frame 0: make the ending state equal the start (no fade), verify loop seam by checking the RMS and waveform continuity across the boundary. Master: -14 LUFS integrated, true peak <= -1 dBTP (4x oversampled peak check), last frames fade to exactly 0. You can't listen, so verify: measure loudness and true peak with ffmpeg ebur128 (peak=true), check the exact sample count, confirm the loop seam is click-free (sample delta at the boundary < 0.01) and bar lines land on frame multiples of 80, check every note fits the chord under it, render a spectrogram PNG and inspect it. Fix and re-render until every check passes, then report the numbers.

metrics.note: Public out.wav downsampled to 32000 Hz for Workers ≤5 MiB; metrics from 48 kHz master.

notes: Seamless 32 s cozy pixel-town loop in G major at 90 BPM with soft pulse lead, kalimba, triangle bass and seaside air. No end fade (loop seam).
